study_identification_part.si_4_title: Comparative analysis of cortical anatomy in male participants with internet gaming disorder or tobacco use disorder: Insights from normative modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used Gaussian process regression (GPR) via the PCNtoolkit (Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit) to generate normative models of cortical thickness development. The normative range was estimated through 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy control group and then applied to patient groups.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit (PCNtoolkit) (https://github.com/predictive-clinical-neuroscience/PCNtool kit-demo.git) was used to estimate a normative model of CT and predict the entire brain based on participants' age and euler index as covariates. The model estimated using Gaussian process regression (GPR) generated, in addition to point estimates, coherent measures of prediction confidence

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness (CT) was calculated from T1-weighted MRI data using surface-based brain morphometry (SBM) in the CAT-12 toolbox. Cortical parcellation was conducted using the Desikan-Killiany atlas, providing regional CT measures.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Surface-based brain morphometry (SBM) was used to calculate CT from T1weighted magnetic resonance imaging data of 804 male participants (665 healthy individuals, 68 IGD and 71 TUD). Gaussian process regression was employed to generate normative models of CT development.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Ma2024.pdf.md: Abstract; Methods and Materials / CT estimation

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age and Euler index as covariates. The Euler index serves as a measure of the reliability of the surface reconstruction and the resulting CT estimates.
